text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
WeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony.
WellAttendedWedding(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
John ::: a specific individual named John.
Premises:
∀x (WeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are engaged.
∀x (Invite(x, y) → WeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others make wedding plans.
∀x (WellAttendedWedding(x) → Invite(x, y)) ::: Anyone with a well-attended wedding invites others.
∃x (LargerFamily(x) ∧ WellAttendedWedding(x)) ::: Some people with larger families have well-attended weddings.
Engaged(John) → (¬Invite(John, y) ∧ ¬WeddingPlans(John)) ::: If John is engaged, then he does not invite friends and does not make wedding plans.
LargerFamily(John) → (WellAttendedWedding(John) ∨ Invite(John, y)) ::: If John has a larger family, then either he has a well-attended wedding or invites friends.
Conclusion:
LargerFamily(John) ::: John has a larger family.
